title: Delta export intake gateway and evidence-driven priority scoring for enterprise console requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers continue to file ad-hoc console reporting and export requests that vary widely (one-off CSV dumps, recurring delta exports, tenant-level cost attributions, and scheduled dashboards). Our current triage is manual, inconsistent, and lacks a reproducible signal for SLA assignment. This creates slow turnarounds for high-value customers and causes engineering thrash.
proposal_summary: Build an intake gateway (web form + API path + handset triage UI) that captures evidence and required signals up-front and applies an evidence-driven priority score to route requests into four SLA lanes (Self-serve, Standard SLA, Enterprise SLA, Escalation). The gateway will produce machine-readable metadata for downstream routing and automations (auto-acknowledgement, estimated ETA, suggested templates). We will support delta exports and scheduled job requests with clear acceptance criteria for export formats, privacy boundaries, and cost attribution mappings.
scoring_rules: Score is a weighted sum of: 1) Customer tier (self-serve=0, standard=2, enterprise=5), 2) Data sensitivity/compliance need (none=0, PII=3, high-regulated=6), 3) Frequency (ad-hoc=0, nightly delta=2, hourly delta=5), 4) Cost sensitivity (low=0, medium=2, high=4), 5) Business criticality provided by customer (none=0, required=4). We will normalize into 0-100 and map thresholds: 0-20 => Self-serve; 21-45 => Standard SLA; 46-75 => Enterprise SLA; 76-100 => Escalation (requires Engineering & CSM review). The form will encourage attachment of evidence (usage dashboard screenshots, query examples, sample output) which increases score weight by +5 if present.
intake_form_fields: Required fields: workspace_id, contact_email, customer_tier, desired_format (CSV/Parquet/JSON), frequency (one-off/nightly/hourly), retention_policy, data_filters (workspaces/tenant IDs), cost_attribution_fields (billable_unit, label_mappings), compliance_flags (PII, GDPR, SOC2), justification/business_impact, sample_row_or_query, preferred_sla. Optional: preferred_time_window, destination (S3/BigQuery/Console-export), config_as_code reference. The form will validate formats and show immediate estimated lane and ETA based on scoring.
sla_lane_map: Self-serve: immediate guidance + self-serve template and docs; Standard SLA: 7-14 business days, managed by analytics ops; Enterprise SLA: 3-7 business days, assigned to an analyst + CSM + optional engineering for automation; Escalation: <72 hours response, includes engineering, security, and account exec. Delta exports: Standard and Enterprise lanes support automated incremental exports. Escalation lane supports proofing and one-off engineering interventions.
success_metrics: 1) 30% reduction in median time-to-first-delivery for enterprise export requests within 90 days. 2) 40% fewer back-and-forth clarifying questions (tracked via intake form completion rate). 3) 25% reduction in engineering triage time per request. 4) >80% accuracy of automatic lane assignment vs. manual reviewer in A/B trial.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers may underreport data sensitivity; mitigation: require explicit compliance flags and sample data redaction checklist. Risk: Overtriage causes engineering load; mitigation: tune scoring thresholds during beta and require manual override with audit trail. Risk: Export destinations introduce security concerns; mitigation: require destination allowlist and security review for new destinations. Risk: Dependencies on analytics export infra (ETL/delta infra); mitigation: stage beta with S3/CSV exports while infra work completes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Working intake form reachable from Console with automated scoring and lane suggestion. 2) Intake form stores metadata in request queue and exposes API for downstream consumers. 3) Automated acknowledgement email template with ETA and required next steps sent on submission. 4) Demo of two scheduled delta exports (nightly and hourly) executed end-to-end into a customer-owned S3 bucket under Standard and Enterprise lanes. 5) Security review completed for export destinations and data handling policy approved.
next_steps: 1) Draft PRD and wireframes (owner: Aisha) by 2026-02-18. 2) Implement form prototype + scoring engine (owner: Marco) by 2026-03-12. 3) Beta launch with three enterprise customers (owner: Lena Hoffman, CSM) starting 2026-03-25. 4) Capture metrics and iterate thresholds for two weeks; decision to promote to GA by 2026-04-30. 5) Post-GA: automate routing into work queues and create runbook for Escalation lane (owner: Ops).
